title: Passwordless Authentication
description: Implement passwordless authentication methods including magic links, WebAuthn, and one-time codes.

data.text: **Passwordless authentication** removes the need for users to remember and type passwords. Instead, users prove identity through something they have (email, phone, security key) or something they are (biometrics).

items: **Reuse**: Users recycle passwords across sites, so one breach compromises many accounts
**Phishing**: Passwords can be stolen via fake login pages
**Brute force**: Weak passwords are guessable with enough attempts
**Credential stuffing**: Leaked passwords are automatically tried on other sites
**Helpdesk burden**: Password resets consume support resources

data.title: The Password Problem
data.text: According to Verizon's DBIR, over 80% of data breaches involve stolen or weak passwords. Passwordless auth eliminates this attack surface entirely.

A **magic link** is a single-use, time-limited URL sent to the user's email. Clicking it logs the user in without requiring a password. The flow is simple but must be implemented with strict security controls.

data.title: Magic Link Generation (C#)
data.content: Generating and validating a secure magic link token in ASP.NET Core

items: Token must be cryptographically random (use `RandomNumberGenerator`, not `Guid` alone)
Token must be single-use (mark `Used = true` after first use)
Rate limit magic link requests per email/IP

data.text: **WebAuthn** is the W3C standard for passwordless authentication using public-key cryptography. Users authenticate with a hardware security key (YubiKey), platform authenticator (Windows Hello, Touch ID), or roaming authenticator (phone).

data.title: Why WebAuthn Is Secure
data.text: WebAuthn is phishing-resistant because the credential is bound to the origin (domain). An attacker cannot replay a credential on a fake site. It also never exposes a private key to the server.

data.caption: Passwordless authentication flow using magic links
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant C as Client App
    participant S as Server
    participant E as Email Provider
    U->>C: Enter email address
    C->>S: Request magic link
    S->>S: Generate secure token
    S->>E: Send email with link
    E->>U: Deliver email
    U->>C: Click magic link
    C->>S: Validate token
    S->>S: Check expiry + single use
    S->>C: Return session/JWT
    C->>U: User is logged in

data.text: OTP codes are numeric or alphanumeric codes sent via email or SMS. They are simpler than magic links but require the user to manually copy-paste. For higher security, combine OTP with a secondary factor.

items.text: Use cryptographically secure random tokens (not sequential or guessable)
items.hint: Prefer RandomNumberGenerator over Guid for token generation

items.text: Set token expiration to 15 minutes or less
items.hint: Longer windows increase the window for interception
Invalidate immediately after first successful use
Users may lose access to their email or security keys
Essential for forensic analysis after incidents

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Magic links require secure, expiring, single-use tokens
WebAuthn is phishing-resistant and uses public-key cryptography
data.takeaway: Passwordless authentication is more secure and user-friendly than passwords when implemented correctly.
